exposure: early initiation of complementary feeding (before 6 months)
cohort: The study included 702 children aged 12-59 months from the Dembecha district.
finding: The prevalence of developmental delay was 26.7%, and it was significantly associated with toddler child age, low birth weight, cesarean section, preterm delivery, early initiation of complementary feeding, stunting, inadequate meal frequency, and inadequate dietary diversity.
mod_finding: Cesarean section mode of delivery was significantly associated with child developmental delay (AOR = 8.60; 95% CI: 3.93, 18.65).
cross-section timing: Children aged 12-59 months at the time of data collection.
